newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt paper price, yield seen at mkt level.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt paper price, yield seen at mkt level.

text.p: Strong demand as investors try to move out of cash over Russia's May Day holidays will drive prices at Wednesday's GKO discount Treasury bills and OFZ interest-bearing bond auctions to secondary-market levels, or add a premium, dealers said on Tuesday.
*Turnover rose to 5.54 trillion from 3.54 trillion roubles
*Central Bank stayed away from the market

Dealers forecast the average yield on the new 322-day bills, which mature on March 18, 1998, would be in a 29.5-30.7 percent range. The series 23003 bills, which mature on March 4 next year, closed with a yield of 30.18 percent.

The forecast the average price of the new 728-day bond, maturing April 28, 1999, in a 95.9-99.0 percent range. The 24011 bond issue, maturing on March 31, 1999, closed at 100.15 to yield 36.04 percent.
"I can see a strong wish to buy and the results (of the auctions) will not differ much from those on the secondary market," a dealer said.

"The Finance Ministry is unlikely to give a big yield, and besides that the next proper secondary trading will only take place on Monday, that's why very few people would like to leave money at the exchange."
After the auctions are over on Wednesday, there will be a one-hour trading session. Usually there is no trading on Wednesdays.

"Unexpected things are unlikely to happen at the auctions -- the results will be in line with the secondary market," MFK bank dealer Andrei Koshchi said. "If there is any premium, it will be a small one, as people may fail to trade after the auctions."
Dealers said prices rose on Tuesday on demand from Russian banks, as most of the gains were in medium-dated issues usually bought by Russian investors.
